question: Who will cause every year, annual financial statement to be laid before the Legislative Assembly of the State?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annual financial statement:-**

 
 
• **In India, the Governor of each state is responsible for causing the annual financial statement to be laid before the Legislative Assembly of the State.**
 
• **This is mandated by Article 202 of the Constitution of India.**
 
• The annual financial statement, also known as the budget, outlines the estimated receipts and expenditures of the state for the upcoming financial year.
 
• The Governor presents the budget to the Legislative Assembly, where it is debated and approved. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President of India:-**

 
 
• **It is the head of state of India and the commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces. **
 
• The President is indirectly elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states and union territories.
 
• The President's term of office is five years.
 
 
 
• **Deputy Chief Minister:-**
 
 
• **It is the second-in-command of the Council of Ministers, after the Prime Minister. **
 
• The Deputy Chief Minister is responsible for assisting the Prime Minister in the administration of the Union government.
 
• The Deputy Chief Minister is also responsible for coordinating the work of the various ministries of the Union government.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister of India:-**
 
 
• **It is the head of government of an Indian state. **
 
• The Chief Minister is elected by the members of the state legislature, and is responsible for leading the state government.
 
• The Chief Minister's powers are executive, legislative, and judicial.
 
• The Chief Minister is responsible for the administration of the state government, and has the power to appoint the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Chief Minister also has the power to veto laws passed by the state legislature, and to grant pardons and reprieves.
